articles.title: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis Found Guilty of Orchestrating Tupac Shakur’s Murder
articles.summary: A jury has found Duane “Keffe D” Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur. After a day of closing arguments, Davis was found guilty of murder with the use of a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang, according to ABC News. body: During his closing arguments, prosecutor Binu Palal said that the case was “drenched in circumstantial evidence” and corroborating witnesses, in addition to Davis’ own statements over the years to media and in his own memoir to show that he was guilty of aiding the murder. “For nearly 18 years, Duane Davis has told the police, television, books, YouTube interviewers — anybody that will listen, he has told — he is responsible for the murder of Tupac Shakur,” said Palal. “Tell him you hear him — find him guilty.”
Davis’ attorney Michael Sanft, meanwhile, argued that the only proof that Davis was responsible for Shakur’s murder was through his own confessions, which did not constitute real evidence.
“We have to ask ourselves the question really at this particular point: Why are we here 30 years later if Duane Davis had actually confessed — truly confessed?” he said.
Davis is scheduled to be sentenced on October 13 and will be held without bail. He shared that he plans to appeal the sentence once it’s handed down.

articles.title: ‘Guardians of the Video Game’ Lands Finecut for International Sales Ahead of Toronto Market
articles.summary: Seoul-based sales agent Finecut has acquired international sales rights to “Guardians of the Video Game,” a 3D animated feature based on the Naver Webtoon of the same name, ahead of the Toronto market.
body: Uhm Young-sik directs the feature, adding to a filmography that includes the animated film “Running Man: Revengers” and the animation portion of “Yumi’s Cells” Season 1. He earlier co-directed “Red Shoes and the Seven Dwarfs,” a title that reached distribution in 120 countries.

Animation and VFX studio Locus Animation produces “Guardians of the Video Game.” The company’s credits include “Red Shoes and the Seven Dwarfs” and “Exorcism Chronicles: The Beginning,” the latter of which now has a sequel in production. Locus Animation has built a broader slate around adaptations of popular webtoons, among them “Barkhan” and “Denma.”
“Guardians of the Video Game” is currently in post-production and slated for release in the fourth quarter of 2026. Its first footage will be revealed through Finecut during the Toronto market.

articles.title: The Rise of ‘Love Island USA’: From Death Threats Against Contestants to Agency Battles for the Biggest Stars
articles.summary: When Liv Walker first heard from the “Love Island USA” casting team, she thought it might be a scam. After all, she had never even seen the show. Originally scouted for Season 5 of the reality dating show, Walker turned down the initial offer.
body: Season 6 went on to transform the U.S. installment of “Love Island,” distinguishing itself from the U.K. version that had popularized the idea of dropping a group of young, ready-to-mingle strangers together into a private villa cut off from the outside world.

“ Love Island USA ” originally aired on CBS when the show launched in 2019, with comedian Arielle Vandenberg hosting. The series switched to Peacock for its fourth season, replacing Vandenberg with Sarah Hyland — before Ariana Madix officially took over as host in Season 6. Following her dramatic break-up with Tom Sandoval, the “Vanderpump Rules” star brought the Bravo audience over to Peacock, and the dynamic cast kept them watching.

Season 6 of “Love Island USA,” which is produced by ITV America and airs on Peacock every summer, saw its viewership double compared to that of previous seasons, according to NBCUniversal. Those numbers have only continued to grow in the two years since. This past summer, Season 8 drew 19 billion minutes watched, translating to 7.9 million views, according to data from Peacock.

articles.title: Trump Endorses U.S. Tax Incentive to Keep Hollywood Production: ‘Let’s Get This Done!’
articles.summary: President Trump on Monday endorsed a federal tax incentive for film and TV production, a move long sought by Hollywood studios and unions. In a statement posted to Truth Social, Trump said he will push for a bipartisan bill to save the industry.
body: Several Democratic lawmakers have gotten behind the idea, notably including Sen. Adam Schiff, who held a hearing on the topic in March. But Schiff and others have said that Republican lawmakers were waiting on a positive signal from the White House getting on board.
Charles Rivkin, the CEO of the Motion Picture Association, applauded Trump’s move in a statement.

“For over a century, American studios, casts, and crews have produced the films and series that the world wants to see,” Rivkin said. “A federal incentive would be a landmark step toward bringing more production to local communities in all 50 states, strengthening our nation’s economy, and making our country a more competitive place to produce, create, and tell great stories. We applaud President Trump’s support for this vital action, and we look forward to continuing to work with the White House and bipartisan leaders in Congress to enact a meaningful and effective national incentive into law.”

Supporters of the measure have cited a dramatic drop in domestic production since the streaming bubble burst in 2022. Around 73,000 jobs have been lost nationwide, about two-thirds of them in Los Angeles.

articles.title: US singer D4vd's celebrity lawyers withdraw from murder case
articles.summary: The singer, 21, will be now represented by a public defender in the murder trial of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. He has pleaded not guilty.
body: The celebrity lawyers hired to represent US musician D4vd in his upcoming murder trial have withdrawn from the case.

The star, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, has been appointed a public defender to mount his defence against the charge of murdering Celeste Rivas Hernandez, 14, whose remains were found in September 2025 in a Tesla registered to his address.
Burke, 21, pleaded not guilty to the murder charges in a Los Angeles court on Monday.
A judge determined last month that he will stand trial for murder. Prosecutors have alleged he stabbed the teen after years of sexual abuse before dismembering her body.

articles.title: ‘Obsession’ Producer Files Lawsuit Claiming She Was Cut Out of Profits Despite “Rescuing” Cut
articles.summary: Producers James Harris and Mark Lane are accused by fellow producer Leonora Ann Darby of making compensation promises that they did not keep when the Curry Barker feature became a massive hit.
body: An executive producer on Obsession who allegedly “rescued“ the box office smash hit from a bad edit is suing two fellow producers for cutting her out of her share of the profits.

In a lawsuit filed in California state court on Monday, producer Leonora Ann Darby accuses Tea Shop Productions‘ co-founders and her colleagues James Harris and Mark Lane of reneging on an agreement to treat her as an equal producer at the company and not acknowledging her key role on Obsession, with financial ramifications.

Though she was formally credited as an executive producer on Obsession, the lawsuit argues Darby acted as a lead producer within the functional, internal definition used by Tea Shop Productions. Conveniently, the lawsuit alleges, once Obsession became a major hit — recently crossing $500 million worldwide on a reported $750,000 budget — she was boxed out of net profit participation previously promised for projects she lead-produced, despite her significant work on the film.

articles.title: ‘Sometimes you just need a good cry’: why Little Women is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our series of writers highlighting their go-to comfort films is an ode to the teary 1994 adaptation of the classic novel. I have an ongoing argument with some friends about how I refuse to watch Interstellar again, despite considering it a beautiful and well-crafted film.
body: But at the same time, the movie I choose as my feelgood film is one that has reduced me to a sobbing, snotty mess time and time again, whether I’m watching it curled up with my cat on the couch, swaddled in blankets while sick in bed or jostling with my seatmate for the armrest on an airplane. And just like with the score from Interstellar, the moment I hear Thomas Newman’s wistful little oboe intro of the 1994 version of Little Women, I can feel my eyes well up with tears.

As you’ve probably discerned already, I tend to feel things very strongly. Probably one of my most psychotic traits is that I have to spoil the endings of most movies before I watch them for the first time because if I get too attached to a character and that character dies, it could take me several days to recover. But sometimes you just need a good cry, and that’s exactly what Gillian Armstrong’s Little Women is for me.

articles.title: Tom Cruise Had A Second Role On One Of His Most Underrated Hits
articles.summary: These days Tom Cruise is also credited as a producer on most of his movies, but he had a different behind-the-scenes credit on 1990's Days of Thunder.
body: Still, Cruise isn't a credit hog. He's fine with being a star and, most of the time nowadays, a producer. But given that his movies have grossed a combined $13 billion at the worldwide box office, he's earned the right to have a say in other areas of production.

There was, however, one instance of Cruise taking a co-story credit, and it was well-deserved considering that it was his idea to hit the racetrack and make "Days of Thunder." He could probably have lobbied for a co-story credit on some of his other movies, but "Days of Thunder" was special for the actor.

Directed by Tony Scott, "Days of Thunder" stars Cruise as NASCAR star Cole Trickle, whose chronic need for speed is both a strength and a near-fatal flaw. His recklessness lands him in the hospital after a horrific crash, but he ultimately develops the skills to drive hard without constantly putting his life (and the lives of others) in jeopardy.

articles.title: Bel review – the powerful life force and haunting absence of a traumatised singer-songwriter
articles.summary: Beldina Odenyo alchemised the pain of exile, loss and racism into music as Heir of the Cursed before her death in 2021, as this attentive tribute explores. Instead of an artist in a booth, a lone amplifier plays the music of singer-songwriter Beldina Odenyo for a cluster of microphones to pick up…
body: Performing under the moniker Heir of the Cursed, a translation of the Tetela name of assassinated Congolese leader Patrice Lumumba, Odenyo was on the verge of bigger recognition at the end of 2021 after a successful performance at Edinburgh’s Usher Hall. But hemmed in by successive Covid lockdowns, the 31-year-old is clearly unwell in a discomfiting backstage interview. Squirming, monosyllabic, she seems to be regressing to the non-verbal state of shock in which she arrived in Dumfriesshire from Kenya as a young child.

articles.title: Victoria Beckham's company makes its first profit after 18 years
articles.summary: Beckham's fashion and beauty business makes a £7.3m operating profit after years of losses.
body: Victoria Beckham's fashion and beauty business has made an operating profit for the first time since she founded it in 2008, the company has said.
Victoria Beckham Holdings Ltd, which is led by the former Spice Girl as creative director, made an operating profit of £7.3m in 2025, accounts show, after years of losses.
"We have all worked hard for a long time for this moment of profitability and growth," Lady Beckham told the Financial Times, external.

"We've been very transparent about the problems that we had in the business but have recovered and are now growing at a sensible pace. After 20 years, people don't look at my brand as a celebrity brand any more."
